title: Traffic surge & safety thoughts (ramp strategy notebook)
content:
Purpose: quick personal notebook for a conservative traffic ramp that tolerates bursts and warms caches without surprising latency or cost. Not a formal runbook — skeletal checklist + heuristics I can copy into a proper doc later.

Context: moving Model-Delta-2025.08 into prod paths with shared cache layer. We want a slow, observable ramp that exercises KV cache warmup, batching dynamics, and autoscaler behavior, with explicit safety gates for fallbacks. This is targeted at dedicated and hosted tiers (where traffic profiles differ).

High-level approach (one-liner): stepwise traffic increases with a short observation window + automatic soft-fallback to older variant when anomaly triggers, plus manual hold points for tricky customers.

Phases (percent of baseline traffic to new model):
- Phase 0 (smoke): 0.5% for 10m — sanity. Verify routing, credentials, basic outputs.
- Phase 1 (initial): 2% for 30m — watch latency and error meters, KV cache warming begins.
- Phase 2 (observation): 10% for 60m — check batching equilibrium and p95 tail shifts.
- Phase 3 (confidence): 25% for 2h — evaluate cost per token delta and regressions on eval prompts.
- Phase 4 (scaled): 60% for 4h — ensure autoscaler behavior stable, check queue depth under peak.
- Phase 5 (full): 100% after sign-off (final manual gate).

Safety triggers (auto):
- error-rate increase > 0.8 percentage points vs baseline for 5 consecutive minutes -> auto-fallback to previous variant.
- p95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline and absolute p95 > 800ms for 10m -> soft-scale back 50% traffic (or route to lower-cost variant).
- token cost spike > 2.5x expected (billing alert) -> throttle new model to 0% and notify billing lead.
- queue wait time > 300ms for 3m -> reduce new traffic by half, scale up GPU pool if capacity available.

Safety triggers (manual hold):
- customer-visible semantic regressions on 3+ prompts in the eval set -> manual rollback, product review.
- any SLO breach on dedicated customer route (SLA violations) -> immediate hold + page SRE.

Observability checklist (what I will watch during each phase):
- p50/p95/p99 latency per route and global.
- token throughput and per-token cost by model variant.
- 5xx and 4xx error breakdown (model runtime vs infra vs client).
- Batching stats: avg batch size, dropped-token ratio, batch latency distribution.
- KV cache hit/miss rates and warmup curve (per node and global).
- Autoscaler actions: scale events, pending pods/instances, and GPU utilization.
- Request histograms by seq-length bucket.
- Traces for slow tails (link to tracing dashboard).

Quick runbook snippets (for myself):
- Pre-ramp: capacity sanity check (autoscaler cooldowns >= 5m, margin of at least 20% free GPUs at peak).
- Pre-ramp: baseline collect — snapshot all key metrics for last 24h, save as baseline tag.
- During ramp: schedule 1:1 with product manager and on-call SRE for first 60m of Phase 2.
- During ramp: annotate dashboards with phase start times (so we can compare).
- Rollback: change routing rule flag to previous model (traffic control UI), confirm traffic shift completed, then monitor 15m.

Version pinning notes:
- For important customer routes, use explicit version pins for 7 days post-full release. Avoid automatic routing heuristics for those.
- Add a label to the older variant (fallback-friendly=true) to ensure it can accept extra load during rollbacks without cold-cache penalties.
- For A/B evaluation, include unique request header so logs/metrics can be sliced per cohort.

Warmup tactics (to reduce initial latency/poor quality):
- Synthetic warmup: send representative prompts at low rate from a controlled worker prior to Phase 1 to seed KV caches.
- Real-user seed: route 0.5% traffic for 10m with higher sampling of long prompts to exercise worst-case execution paths.
- Preload embeddings/caches for heavy-use routes where embeddings lookup is common.

Interactions to watch (risky spots):
- Increased batching can reduce unit cost but amplify tail latency — be prepared to trade cost for latency during sensitive windows.
- Quantized model variant might lower cost but introduce subtle quality regressions; keep small eval set focused on failure modes.
- Cross-customer cache pollution: check per-tenant cache isolation metrics if we see odd quality dips.

Coordination checklist (who I will ping):
- SRE on-call (Luca) — page threshold and during Phase 2.
- Product (Priya) — sign-off at Phase 3.
- Solutions eng — heads-up for top-10 customers.
- Support — prepare canned responses for rollback scenarios.
- Billing — alert if cost threshold hit.

Open questions / TODOs (my quick backlog):
- TODO: agree exact numeric thresholds with SRE (I guessed the ones above; need to validate).
- TODO: carve out a short eval set of 50 edge prompts for semantic regression checks; assign owner.
- Question: do we want auto-snapshot of KV cache state before Phase 1? Might be heavy.
- TODO: add small script to convert weighted traffic changes into exact router API calls (I keep doing manual math).

Quick template for Slack announcement: 
- "Rolling Model-Delta-2025.08 -> phased ramp starting 2025-04-20 10:00 PDT. Phases: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%. Watch <dashboards>, paging conditions: error-rate +0.8pp / p95 +40% / cost x2.5. Ping @oncall if you see anomalies."

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep ramps conservative on weekdays 10:00–18:00 in primary regions; avoid EOD.
- If rollout crosses major holiday/weekend, force manual opt-in for product sign-off.
- Save a copy of this with the exact metric snapshots we collect during Phase 2 — useful for postmortem.

End.
